'''Knoephla''' are dumplings commonly used in [[Cookbook:Knoephla soup|knoephla soup]], a popular dish in the American Midwest.

==Ingredients==
*2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (500 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] (5 ml) [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]
*½ cup (250 ml) [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] or water

==Procedure==
#In a mixing bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, egg, and then the milk or water. Mix to form a firm [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] that is not sticky. Add a bit more flour if needed to keep dough from being sticky or a bit more liquid if too dry.
#Roll pieces of dough between the hands to the length of a pencil (6 [[Cookbook:Inch|in]] / 15 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]). Snip off small pieces with a knife or scissors.
#Use the knoephla as specified in your given recipe.
